Role Summary Join Coca-Cola's Global Equipment Platforms team and help shape the future of iconic products-like Freestyle fountain dispensers, coolers, vending machines, and our digital apps. This is your opportunity to combine modern UI design skills with systems thinking for experiences that touch millions worldwide.

We're a highly collaborative, innovative, in-office team passionate about growth, consumer insights, and blazing new trails in digital equipment.

Key Responsibilities Design pixel-perfect user interfaces for equipment displays (Freestyle, vending machines, coolers), embedded screens, web applications, and mobile apps (iOS & Android) Deliver high-fidelity UI designs and interactive prototypes using Figma, clearly communicating user flows, states, and interactions, while aligning every detail with established UI guidelines and specifications.

Use component libraries, variants, and responsive design principles to ensure scalable, consistent solutions across platforms Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams-including software engineers, digital product leads, and fellow designers-by participating in in-office collaboration, design jams, and hands-on field visits for direct observations and interviews.

Support UX research by participating in user observations, interviews, and feedback sessions-translating insights into actionable UI improvements. Document UI specifications, standards, and design system components for seamless development handoff.

Contribute to, refine, and champion our UI Design System and global brand standards, ensuring consistency, scalability, and outstanding visual quality across platforms. Confidently present, explain, and defend your design decisions to peers, leadership, and partners-while actively seeking and embracing constructive feedback.

Key Deliverables Pixel-perfect, production-ready UI designs and interactive prototypes in Figma. Clear, detailed UI specifications, component documentation, and design system updates. Actionable insights and recommendations informed by user fieldwork and observation. Compelling design presentations and storytelling to stakeholders and collaborators.

Required Skills & Competencies Bachelor's degree in interaction design, HCI, visual communication, graphic/industrial design, or equivalent professional experience. 5+ years of hands-on design experience for digital products (embedded/IoT devices a strong plus).

Expert-level proficiency in Figma (including component shared libraries, variants, interactive prototyping, responsive workflows, design systems) for designing high-fidelity UIs and interactive prototypes.

Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign) Prototyping, wireframing, visual design, sketching, ideation, color theory, typography, and documentation. Proven ability to deliver and iterate on highly polished interfaces.

Effective communicator who confidently presents and defends design decisions, accepting and integrating feedback. Effective collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, especially in face-to-face and workshop environments. Driven by empathy for the user and a relentless focus on creating delightful, impactful experiences.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, collaborative environment Preferred Skills & Competencies Familiarity with front-end technologies (e.g., HTML/CSS/JS) to facilitate effective collaboration with developers. Experience designing for embedded systems, IoT devices, or equipment interfaces.

Experience working with agile development processes and rapid iteration cycles. Knowledge of accessibility standards and best practices. Leadership & Culture Fit Collaborative mindset-thrives in team settings where sharing, supporting, and learning from each other is the norm.

Growth-minded, creative, and always curious-driven to learn, improve, and innovate Consumer-obsessed- relentlessly focused on what delights, inspires, and improves user experience Flexible, proactive, and energized by hands-on, in-office teamwork and direct user engagement.

Fun, bold, and passionate about digital transformation and cutting-edge technology. You will be required to share a portfolio showcasing impactful work on embedded, mobile, and/or web platforms. In addition, you will be required to demonstrate Figma capabilities through sharing files or demonstrating skills.

Make your mark in a global team where innovation is the standard, and your curiosity will always be rewarded. Ready to shape the future of digital experiences? Apply now!

You'll work alongside engineers and product managers to create experiences used daily by millions of users. What You'll Own Design beautiful and intuitive interfaces for iOS and Android applications. Create wireframes, user flows, prototypes and production-ready UI.

Design mobile experiences across insurance, payments, claims, investments and financial services. Build and maintain mobile design systems and reusable components. Work closely with developers to ensure pixel-perfect implementation. Optimize interfaces for usability, accessibility and platform guidelines.

Iterate designs using analytics, usability findings and product feedback. Ensure consistency across different devices, screen sizes and operating systems. Deep understanding of iOS Human Interface Guidelines and Android Material Design. Strong understanding of mobile usability, responsive layouts and interaction design. Excellent attention to typography, spacing, colour and visual hierarchy. Ability to simplify complex financial workflows into clean mobile experiences. Portfolio is required.

Design Stack Figma FigJam Design Systems Auto Layout Interactive Prototyping iOS Human Interface Guidelines Material Design The Kind of Builder We Want Thinks mobile-first. Obsesses over visual polish and interaction quality. Notices small UI inconsistencies before users do. Cares about accessibility, responsiveness and performance.

This is a senior design leadership role at a fast-growing, Sequoia- and Index-backed AI procurement platform serving large industrial companies across Europe. The company is at Series A/B stage with ~150 employees and is rethinking how procurement works — combining human expertise with AI agents to make high-impact cost decisions legible, trustworthy, and actionable for industrial buyers.
As Head of Product Design , you will define how humans and AI agents collaborate across the product, build and lead a team of ~4 product designers, and establish design as a true strategic partner alongside product and engineering. This role has direct impact on profitability for large industrial customers and shapes the future of agent-native enterprise UX.
Location: Munich, Germany (hybrid on-site). No visa sponsorship available — right to work in Germany is required.

Define the interaction paradigm for an agent-native product, where AI agents execute procurement workflows and buyers supervise, steer, and handle exceptions.
Turn a screen-first product into an agent-driven experience — building the mental models, UI patterns, and frameworks that make complex decisions legible and trustworthy for non-analyst users.
Translate technical procurement concepts (e.g. should-costing, raw material indices, contract leakage) into accessible, actionable UX.
Own and evolve the design system and component architecture to support agent-driven development and rapid iteration.
Build, hire, and lead a team of ~4 product designers — setting standards for craft, speed, and strategic impact.
Establish design as a strategic partner in the product trio alongside product management and engineering.
Drive company-wide user understanding through UX research best practices and ongoing advocacy for real user problems.
Collaborate closely with executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders (PM, Engineering, C-suite).

6+ years of product design experience, with at least 2+ years in design leadership and people management at high-growth technology companies.
Deep experience designing data-heavy, workflow-driven products — able to make information density an asset rather than a liability.
Proven ability to build and maintain design systems and component architectures for complex software products.
Genuine fluency with AI as a design material — a clear, articulate point of view on LLMs, agents, and automation in product UX.
Demonstrated experience designing UX for AI/LLM-driven products and agent-driven workflows, translating complex AI concepts into clear UI for non-experts.
Strong systems thinking: you design in frameworks and patterns, not just individual screens.
Demonstrated ability to move fluidly between strategic leadership and hands-on craft.
Strong collaborator with product and engineering, with solid stakeholder management and communication skills up to C-suite level.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Design, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related field.
Fluent in English (written and spoken).

German language skills (not required).
Background in enterprise procurement, supply chain, or industrial software domains.
Experience at companies recognised for design excellence.
Location & Work Arrangement
Location: Munich, Bavaria, Germany
Work arrangement: Hybrid on-site (Munich office)
Visa sponsorship: Not available — candidates must have the right to work in Germany

A Series A-stage AI/ML SaaS scaleup in the procurement intelligence and supply chain management space, headquartered in Munich. The platform serves large industrial customers across Europe, using AI agents to automate and optimise procurement workflows — from spend and cost intelligence to supplier management, sourcing, and compliance. Backed by top-tier European and global venture investors, the team is ~150 people strong and growing fast.

KAYAK, part of Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), is the world’s leading travel search engine. With billions of queries across our platforms, we help people find their perfect flight, stay, rental car and vacation package. We’re also transforming business travel with a new corporate travel solution, KAYAK for Business.
As an employee of KAYAK, you will be part of a travel company that operates a portfolio of global metasearch brands including momondo, Cheapflights and HotelsCombined, among others. From start-up to industry leader, innovation is in our DNA and every employee has an opportunity to make their mark. Our focus is on building the best travel search engine to make it easier for everyone to experience the world.
KAYAK is seeking a Staff Product Designer, Mobile to own the design direction across our apps and lead the craft of every designer who works on them.

This is a senior individual contributor role with manager-level scope: you carry the design direction and UX/UI patterns across three teams (Apps Meta, Apps Retention, and Mobile Design Systems) while still designing and shipping yourself.

You set the quality bar for all Apps design output, you hold it across teams, and you keep engineering pointed at the right work. You are the technical lead for apps design, accountable for the quality and velocity of what the apps designers produce, without managing them directly.
This role is required to work from our Berlin office 3 days per week.

Own the design direction and the UX/UI pattern system across the apps surface. Navigation, mental models, and UI consistency cut across Apps Meta, Retention, and Design Systems at once, and you hold that cross-cutting direction so three teams ship one coherent experience rather than three versions of it.
Set the quality standard for apps design and hold it as a discipline, not a project. Make the bar visible where teams miss it, and close gaps across teams that you did not personally create. You are accountable for the quality and velocity of all apps design output.
Run planning and discovery for all three teams. Break multi-team, loosely defined problems into clear design direction the designers can run with.
Partner with the Director of Product for Apps and the apps PMs on core initiatives, influencing roadmap and prioritization through design rationale.
Lead native craft across iOS and Android. Set the approach for resizability, foldables, new screen sizes, and solve how KAYAK responds to platform chrome shifts like Liquid Glass and Material 3 Expressive.
Lead the design approach for mobile AI features: how we integrate AI into the apps, the UI, and the navigation around it, so it lands as a native part of the experience.
Drive the brand differentiation work for our portfolio of hero brands apps like momondo to ensure local market dominance.
Raise the ceiling for the other apps designers through critique, shared standards, and patterns they build on. Designers should get better by working alongside you and using what you establish, not only through direct mentorship.
Required Skills
10+ years in product design, with a portfolio of shipped, high-impact mobile work at consumer scale.
Deep native expertise across iOS and Android. Mastery of Apple HIG and Material Design, and the judgment to know when to converge and when to honor platform difference. Hands-on experience with resizability, foldables, and iPad, and a point of view on platform chrome directions like Liquid Glass and Material 3 Expressive.
A track record of raising design quality across a discipline beyond your own projects, through standards you set, critiques you ran, or systems others still use.
Experience driving design direction across multiple teams or product areas, with the ability to influence without authority.
Experience building or evolving mobile design systems and scalable patterns.
Strong with Figma, and fluent with AI-assisted design and prototyping tooling (for example Claude Code or Cursor).

Founding Product Designer
At Adclear, we're building the trust layer for how the world's most regulated companies bring products to market. Every bank, lender and investment platform runs into the same invisible pain: compliance review that slows down every campaign, every launch, every idea. We're turning the function that has always said 'no' into infrastructure that says 'yes, and here's how'.
This is a fundamental shift in how regulated industries and compliance teams operate, and we're only at the beginning. The product you'll design is what people actually touch when they experience that shift.
Founded in 2024, we've already earned the trust of leading innovators as well as established enterprises including Monzo, Lloyds, PensionBee, Kraken, Coinbase and many others. Our early traction let us raise 2.6m in funding, and we're now scaling fast. We're building the product engine that turns a genuinely novel category into something people love to use, and this is where you come in.
The Basics
Location: London (4 days a week in our Farringdon office)
Reports to: founders, working day to day alongside our CTO
The role: our first dedicated designer, owning the product experience end to end

You'd be the first designer at Adclear. Today, design here is developer-led and largely AI/vibe-coded, with no single owner. That's the gap you're filling: the product's look, feel and flow are yours to mold, and the design function is yours to build from the ground up.
This role has two distinct halves, and we're looking for someone who can genuinely do both.
The first is improving what already exists. Adclear is a live product used regularly by enterprises and other customers. You'll bring coherence to the UI, refine and properly apply our existing design system across the app, improve existing functionality, and design complex new features on top of it. Strong UX judgment matters as much as UI polish here: a lot of this is making genuinely complex, regulated workflows navigable for non-technical users like compliance reviewers and marketers.
The second is zero-to-one. We'll likely be building two new product lines from scratch alongside the core product, which means heavy discovery, lots of proof-of-concepts, and rapid iteration through quick mockups, AI-assisted prototypes and user testing. You'll be speaking with customers regularly across both workstreams, not just the new ones.
You won't be handed tidy specs and asked to make them pretty. You'll sit in the messy middle: talking to compliance teams and marketers at banks and fintechs, working out what they actually need, and turning genuinely hard, ambiguous problems into a product that feels obvious once it exists.
This is a design role with a real product management edge. You'll work in tandem with our CTO to shape what we build and why, not just how it looks. You'll help set priorities, scope releases and make the calls that move the roadmap.

We’re a well-funded startup building category-defining AI for architecture, engineering and construction: an archaic industry at a critical juncture. The Building Safety Act now requires firms to evidence their design decisions, and directors carry personal liability.
Join Bite as our first in-house designer working strategically and directly with the head of product, founders and engineering team, you’ll own the entire design function and lead the transformation of our beta into a high-quality user experience that shapes the future of Bite’s AI for the built environment.

The problem is genuinely hard. When a structural engineer changes a component in their building design model, the same component exists in drawings, schedules, specs and emails under different names, in different formats, some of which LLMs don’t understand, and with no shared identifier. Detecting these changes, predicting the downstream impacts and propagating them using AI under the engineer's supervision is the core of our product.
You'll own the UX/UI for the whole product, not a slice of it. There's no design team to inherit and no feature factory to work around. You set the direction, the patterns and the quality bar, and you'll prototype, test and ship rapidly with a small team that can pivot, fast.
Your work ships to people who pay. The beta is in production with signed customers that include some of the UK's leading structural engineering firms who are keen to build with us. With our tight feedback loops, you’ll have plenty of data to help drive your design decisions.
What we're building
Structural engineers work across numerous, fragmented sets of tools with no shared source of truth. When a design changes, propagating that change across files is manual, slow and error-prone, and the errors are expensive.
Bite is the change management and audit trail layer for structural engineering. The platform does three things that today take weeks of manual work: natural-language search across a project's entire file ecosystem, cross-file impact detection e.g. "I changed Column C7 in the structural model - what drawings, schedules, and specs are now out of date?" and propagation of those changes to every affected file.
